source.section_read: What is a good INP score?
source.tool: Claude in Chrome — mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate + javascript_tool (read-only innerText slice; no clicks, no consent interaction, no downloads)
source.staleness_note_our_words: The page's own last-updated date is 2025-09-02, one year to the day before this read. The figures below are current as of that page revision, not necessarily current forever — this is a conclusions-are-debt row (s129-D5) and wants a re-check date.

good.boundary_our_words: 200 ms or less is good responsiveness.
good.receipt: "An INP below or at 200 milliseconds means a page has good responsiveness."

needs_improvement.boundary_our_words: Above 200 ms and up to 500 ms needs improvement.
needs_improvement.receipt: "An INP above 200 milliseconds and below or at 500 milliseconds means a page's responsiveness"

poor.receipt: "An INP above 500 milliseconds means a page has poor responsiveness."

the_percentile_the_threshold_is_stated_a.our_words: The threshold is not a per-interaction budget. It is stated at the 75th percentile of page loads recorded in the FIELD, and segmented separately for mobile and desktop.
the_percentile_the_threshold_is_stated_a.receipt: "a good threshold to measure is the 75th percentile of page loads recorded in the field"
the_percentile_the_threshold_is_stated_a.why_it_matters_our_words: A lab measurement on one machine cannot satisfy this threshold, and neither can a mean. Any Apollo claim about INP has to name the population, the percentile and the device class, or it is not the same measurement the standard describes. Mobile and desktop are separate verdicts, not one blended number.

the_page_s_own_hedge.our_words: The page opens the section by conceding that labelling a responsiveness metric 'good' or 'poor' is difficult, because device capability varies enormously across the people using a site. The thresholds are a deliberate compromise between encouraging good practice and staying achievable.
the_page_s_own_hedge.receipt: "there's considerable variability in the capabilities of devices people use"
the_page_s_own_hedge.consequence_our_words: Carry the hedge into the graph with the number. A principle node that states 200 ms without the 75th-percentile-of-field qualifier will be cited as a per-interaction target, which is what the page is arguing against.

bearing_on_r1_idea_11.our_words: R1's idea 11 proposed a response budget in the behaviour contract — acknowledge within 100 ms, plus a declared policy for showing work on delegated tasks — and named this UNPROVEN item as its blocker. The blocker is now cleared for the INP half. The 100 ms acknowledge figure is a DIFFERENT claim from a different source and is NOT proved by this addendum.
bearing_on_r1_idea_11.status: idea 11's INP dependency: MET. Its 100 ms dependency: still unproved, not chased by this lane.
